Strategy: Tiny items go loose, the rest go tight. An item far smaller than bins barely dents any of them, so put it in the loosest bin and keep tight bins untouched for items that fit them. Score by residual when the item is under a quarter of the tightest residual, else Best Fit, so ranking can switch only for tiny items. It may help by consolidating them, but may fail by cluttering the loosest bin while tight bins strand.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    tiny = item * 4 <= min(bins)
    return [r if tiny else -(r - item) for r in bins]
```
generator_note: Tiny-item worst-fit: loosest bin when item*4 <= min residual, else Best Fit.
